findings.finding: The plan claims that calling reconfigure(encoding="utf-8") on stdout and stderr in `main` makes rebar's output UTF-8 on every host with no downside. It doesn't look at in-repo parent processes that run the rebar CLI as a subprocess and decode its stdout with the locale codec (`text=True`, no `encoding`). The reconciler runs `rebar list --full` and `rebar show --include-provenance` this way. Those commands print JSON with `ensure_ascii=False`. After the fix, the child writes UTF-8 bytes. On Windows the parent decodes them as cp1252, so non-ASCII ticket titles turn into mojibake (é → Ã©) and the reconciler feeds that to Jira sync. Before the fix, both sides used cp1252, which matched for cp1252-representable text. None of the 22 listed sites cover these consumers, because PLW1514 does not flag text=True (the plan says so itself).
scenarios: A Windows reconciler pass on a ticket titled 'Café rollout': the child writes UTF-8 'Caf\xc3\xa9', the parent decodes it as cp1252 to 'CafÃ©', and the outbound differ sees a title change and pushes the corrupted title to Jira.

findings.finding: Making the CLI write UTF-8 to stdout/stderr changes what every parent process receives from rebar. The plan doesn't list the product code that spawns rebar and reads its output with the locale codec. reclaim_dry_run.py runs `python -m rebar verify-identity --all` with capture_output=True, text=True and no encoding. On Windows that parent will decode the child's new UTF-8 bytes as cp1252. Today child and parent agree on cp1252. After the change, non-ASCII output comes out garbled, and UTF-8 sequences containing bytes cp1252 leaves undefined (0x81/0x8D/0x8F/0x90/0x9D, e.g. U+201D → E2 80 9D) raise UnicodeDecodeError inside subprocess.run.
scenarios: `rebar reclaim --dry-run` (or whatever drives reclaim_dry_run) on a Windows host where verify-identity output contains a typographic quote or dash: the parent raises UnicodeDecodeError, or _verdict_counts parses garbled text.

findings.finding: Reconfiguring sys.stdout/sys.stderr to UTF-8 in `main` changes rebar's output byte contract on Windows. The plan describes it only as 'a no-op on Linux/macOS and under pytest capture'. It does not acknowledge or audit Windows consumers that decode rebar's piped output with the locale codec. Such consumers include in-repo tests/scripts using `subprocess.run([... 'rebar' ...], text=True)` without `encoding`, or hooks/PowerShell capturing output. Before the change, cp1252-representable characters such as the em dash round-tripped. After it, they become mojibake, or raise UnicodeDecodeError on bytes 0x81/0x8d/0x8f/0x90/0x9d. The change also deliberately overrides a user's explicit PYTHONIOENCODING.
scenarios: Windows platform: a repo test or script runs `subprocess.run(['rebar', ...], text=True)`. Output containing an em dash, which previously encoded fine as cp1252 0x97, now arrives as UTF-8 e2 80 94. It decodes to 'â€”', and string assertions fail; bytes like 0x9d raise UnicodeDecodeError.
Windows workstation: a PowerShell user captures `$out = rebar ...`. The output is decoded with [Console]::OutputEncoding (OEM), so non-ASCII text that was previously correct is now mojibake.

findings.finding: The plan's rationale for the BindingRepository probe misstates the stdlib mechanism. `_pyio.TextIOWrapper` reads `os.linesep` once, when the wrapper is constructed (`_configure` sets `self._writenl = newline or os.linesep`), not at write time.
